agents.secrets_warning: The API key and private key are shown ONCE and cannot be retrieved later. Store them securely.
agents.private_key_note: The private key stays with the agent; the server keeps only the public half to verify signatures.
agents.key_mode_agent: The agent uses its own key (recommended) — paste its public key
agents.key_mode_server: Generate a key pair here (quick start)
agents.public_key_hint: Generate it where the agent runs: python tools/provenza_sign.py keygen. The private key never leaves the agent, so Provenza cannot sign in its name.
agents.key_server_note: This key pair was generated by the server: it is not stored, but the server held the private key at that moment. Replace it with an agent-held key for signatures that do not depend on trusting the server.
agents.key_agent_note: Registered as an agent-held key: per the server's records, the private key never reached it. The fingerprint is what an auditor checks.
agents.key_fingerprint_hint: Give this fingerprint to whoever audits the agent: they compare it with the one shown when they verify a signature.
agents.key_replace: Register the agent's own public key
agents.key_replace_hint: The new key replaces the current one for new signatures. Records already signed keep verifying with the key that signed them; the change is written to the audit log.
agents.key_set_failed: Could not set the signing key.
agents.hybrid_hint: Every signature is made with both keys and is valid only if both verify, so a forgery has to break Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204). ML-DSA stays secure against quantum computers that would break elliptic curves.
agents.pq_public_key_hint: Generate both keys where the agent runs: python tools/provenza_sign.py keygen --hybrid. Neither private key leaves the agent.
agents.pq_public_key_replace_hint: Optional. With it the agent signs with the hybrid scheme; leave empty for Ed25519 only (refused when the organization requires post-quantum signatures).
agents.pq_private_key_note: The agent needs both private keys: provenza_sign.py sign PRIVATE_KEY FILE --pq-private-key SEED.
agents.revoke_hint: Revocation is final and public (revocation list, audit log). Signatures received from the moment you give - or from now - are no longer trusted; earlier ones keep verifying.
agents.revoke_hint_current: This is the agent's current key: after revoking it the agent cannot sign, and cannot act, until it registers a new key. Signatures received from the moment you give - or from now - are no longer trusted.
agents.no_key_hint: This agent has no signing key: its actions cannot be verified. Issue a re-key token below.
agents.current_key_revoked_banner: The agent's current key is revoked: its signatures are not trusted. Issue a re-key token, or suspend the agent.

agents.confirm_reactivate: Switch "{{name}}" back on? It will be able to act again with its key.
agents.status_change_failed: Could not change the agent's status.
agents.retired_note: This agent is retired: it cannot act and no longer counts toward a team or role. Its history is kept.

breaker.overrides_hint: An override applies to chains started by that agent (the root of the chain) — e.g. a busy support agent can get a higher attempt limit.

help.window_seconds: How far back events are counted
help.max_denials: Actions refused by policy — catches an agent pushing against its limits
help.max_attempts: Every action check — catches a runaway loop

registry.title: Tool Registry
registry.hint: Which tools, MCP servers and SDKs your agents may use, pinned to a version and manifest digest (OWASP ASI04). A tool that changes after approval is flagged as drifted.
registry.load_failed: Could not load the Tool Registry.
registry.mode_monitor_hint: Nothing is blocked except explicitly blocked tools. Every new tool an agent uses is added here as pending, so the registry fills itself from real traffic. Drift is flagged and raises an incident.
registry.mode_enforce_hint: Only approved tools run. Pinned tools must report a matching version / manifest digest; a drifted tool is refused until re-approved.
registry.confirm_enforce: Switch to enforce? Only approved tools will run. {{count}} entries are not approved yet.
registry.digest_hint: Paste a tool manifest (e.g. an MCP server's tools/list result). The canonical SHA-256 ignores key order and whitespace, so your agents' runtime reports the same value.
registry.digest_invalid_json: The manifest is not valid JSON.
registry.required_capabilities_hint: An agent may call this tool only if it holds these capabilities in its delegation chain. Agents can no longer declare them.

behavior.title: Behavior Monitor
behavior.hint: Each agent is compared with its own recent behaviour: new tools, bursts of activity, runs of denials, unusual hours (OWASP ASI10). In enforce mode a strongly deviating agent is quarantined until an admin releases it.
behavior.load_failed: Could not load the behaviour monitor.
behavior.confirm_release: Release this agent? Its actions will be evaluated normally again.
behavior.mode_monitor_hint: Deviations are recorded here; nothing is blocked.
behavior.mode_enforce_hint: An agent whose score reaches the threshold is quarantined: all its actions are refused and the chains it started are halted.
behavior.confirm_enforce: Switch to enforce? Agents whose score reaches the threshold will be quarantined automatically and every action they attempt will be refused until an admin releases them.
behavior.field_min_samples: Attempts before a baseline is trusted
behavior.help_threshold: Sum of signal weights that triggers quarantine
behavior.help_min_samples: Until then new tools and unusual hours are not flagged
behavior.help_baseline_days: How much history forms the baseline

injection.title: Prompt Injection
injection.hint: Instructions hidden in data can hijack an agent's goal (OWASP ASI01). Tool arguments are scanned on every check, tool outputs on every record. In enforce mode an injected argument is refused, and an injected output taints its chain: further actions in it need a human approval until an admin clears the taint.
injection.load_failed: Could not load the injection guard.
injection.confirm_clear: Clear the taint? Actions in this chain will no longer need a human approval because of the injected output.
injection.tester_placeholder: Paste a web page, e-mail or tool output…
injection.truncated: Only the first 100,000 characters were scanned.
injection.mode_monitor_hint: Detections are recorded here and noted in the decision reason; nothing is blocked. An injected tool output raises an incident.
injection.mode_enforce_hint: An argument with an injection is refused. An injected tool output taints the chain: every further action in it needs a human approval until an admin clears it.
injection.confirm_enforce: Switch to enforce? Tool calls whose arguments contain an injection will be refused, and every chain that receives an injected tool output will need human approval for each further action until an admin clears it.
injection.help_threshold: Lower catches more, with more false positives

codeexec.title: Code Execution
codeexec.hint: An agent that can reach a shell, an interpreter or a database can be steered into running code nobody intended (OWASP ASI05). Every tool call's arguments are checked for reverse shells, pipe-to-shell downloads, eval, SQL injection, path traversal and similar shapes.
codeexec.load_failed: Could not load the code-execution guard.
codeexec.review_only: Code tool call sent for review
codeexec.mode_monitor_hint: Findings are recorded here and noted in the decision reason; nothing is blocked.
codeexec.mode_enforce_hint: Critical findings are refused; high findings and calls to code tools wait for a human approval; medium findings are recorded.
codeexec.confirm_enforce: Switch to enforce? Calls with critical code (reverse shells, pipe-to-shell, disk wipes…) will be refused, and calls with high-risk code or to code tools will wait for a human approval.
codeexec.approve_code_tools: Every code-tool call needs a human approval (enforce)
codeexec.approve_code_tools_hint: Turn off only if code tools run in an isolated sandbox; critical findings are still refused.
codeexec.code_tools_hint: Glob patterns such as shell.* or *.exec. Arguments of these tools are read as commands.

memory.title: Memory Integrity
memory.hint: Whatever lands in an agent's memory comes back into prompts later (OWASP ASI06). Agents attest each memory write and verify retrieved memory before using it; content is scanned for injections and code. Only trusted memory reaches a prompt.
memory.confirm_revoke_entry: Revoke this memory entry? Agents will stop using it at their next verification.
memory.mode_off_hint: Nothing is checked; everything is trusted.
memory.mode_monitor_hint: Findings are recorded; nothing is quarantined or rejected.
memory.mode_enforce_hint: Poisoned chunks and memory entries are quarantined and kept out of prompts; writes into foreign namespaces, by non-active agents or from tainted chains are rejected or quarantined.
memory.confirm_enforce: Switch to enforce? Poisoned memory entries will be quarantined and kept out of prompts, and writes into foreign namespaces will be rejected.
memory.shared_hint: Every agent may write and read these. Its own namespace agent.<id> is always allowed.
memory.ttl_hint: After this an entry verifies as expired (1–365)

a2a.title: Agent Messages
a2a.hint: Agents that talk to each other can be impersonated, replayed or fed altered messages (OWASP ASI07). Each message is registered with an envelope signed by the sender's key and verified again by the recipient before it acts: identity, freshness, single use, allowed route and unaltered content.
a2a.confirm_release: Release this message? The recipient will be allowed to act on it.
a2a.channels_hint: Routes allowed in addition to agents sharing a delegation chain. Disabled channels stay in the list for the audit trail.
a2a.confirm_disable: Disable this channel? In enforce mode these agents will no longer be able to message each other unless they share a chain.
a2a.mode_monitor_hint: Problems are recorded and messages still pass - except replayed nonces and altered payloads, which are never usable.
a2a.mode_enforce_hint: Any failed check rejects the message and raises an incident; a poisoned payload is quarantined until an admin releases it.
a2a.confirm_enforce: Switch to enforce? Messages with an invalid signature, a reused nonce, a stale timestamp or no allowed route will be rejected, and poisoned payloads quarantined. Make sure the channels your agents need exist first.
a2a.allow_same_chain: Agents in the same delegation chain may message each other
a2a.allow_same_chain_hint: Off: only explicit channels are allowed.
a2a.help_message_ttl_seconds: After this the recipient can no longer accept it

identity.title: Agent Identity
identity.hint: Each agent authenticates with its own key (header X-Agent-Key). A key works only on agent endpoints, only for its own agent, and never opens admin pages. Actions run on behalf of the agent's owner, or an admin if it has none.
identity.shown_once: Shown only once - store it in the agent's secret store now.
identity.confirm_rotate: Issue a new key for this agent? The current key keeps working until the grace period ends.
identity.confirm_revoke: Revoke this agent's key now? It will be refused immediately until a new key is issued.
identity.confirm_require: Require agent keys? Agents that still call Provenza with a user's token will be refused on check, record, delegate, messages, memory and the gateway. Make sure every agent has its key first.
identity.require_hint: A user's session can no longer call check, record, delegate, messages, memory or the gateway in an agent's name. The UI keeps working.
identity.grace_hint: How long the old key keeps working after a rotation (0–1440)
identity.require_pq_hint: New agents and key changes must use the hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 scheme; agents without a hybrid key (Ed25519-only or no signing key) cannot delegate, record actions or send messages until they get one.
identity.confirm_require_pq: Require post-quantum signatures? Agents without a hybrid key (Ed25519-only or no signing key) will have their delegations, actions and messages refused until they get one.
identity.confirm_relax: Relax agent identity? A user session will be able to act in an agent's name, or agents without a signing key will be able to act unsigned - neither can be verified later. Every change is in the audit log.
identity.relaxed_warning: Agent identity is relaxed in this organization:
identity.relaxed_session: user sessions can act in an agent's name
identity.relaxed_keyless: agents without a signing key can act unsigned
identity.relaxed_hint: What they do cannot be verified later. Turn it back on in Settings below once your agents use their own keys.
identity.allow_keyless: Allow agents without a signing key (not recommended)
identity.allow_keyless_hint: Off by default: an agent without a signing key cannot delegate or record actions, because nothing it does could be verified later. Turn on only temporarily, while agents get their keys.
identity.relaxed_direct: agents and keys can be registered without proof of possession
identity.allow_direct: Allow registration without proof of possession (not recommended)
identity.allow_direct_hint: Off by default: agents join with a one-time enrollment token and prove they hold their key; keys change only with proof. On: admins can register agents and replace keys directly, as before.

gateway.title: AI Gateway
gateway.hint: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint for agents. Point an agent's base URL here and use its own key: every call is checked against its allowed models, the Prompt Firewall (PII masked before it leaves), prompt-injection in tool messages, rate limits, and the answer is checked for injected instructions and dangerous code.
gateway.connect_hint: The key is the agent's key from Agent Identity (sent as Bearer or X-Agent-Key). Streaming is not supported yet.
gateway.routes_hint: Which connection serves a model name. A pattern such as gpt-4o* is allowed; an exact name wins over a pattern. The agent must also have the model in its allowed models.
gateway.routes_empty: No routes - the gateway serves no model yet.
gateway.confirm_disable: Disable this route? Agents asking for this model will get 'model not routed'.
gateway.enabled_hint: Off: every gateway call is refused.
gateway.scan_output_hint: Scan answers for injected instructions (ASI01) and critical code (ASI05); in enforce mode such an answer is replaced.
gateway.blocked_terms_moved: Kept on their own page now, with scopes (all agents, a team, an agent...):

queue.title: Queue & Retention
queue.hint: AI requests run in a background queue. A request that waits too long is not sent late: it expires. A request delivered to the worker twice is processed once. Requests nobody approves expire, and encrypted raw prompts can be wiped after a retention period. A sweep enforces this every 5 minutes.
queue.sweeps_empty: No sweep has changed anything yet.
queue.queue_ttl_hint: A queued request that has not started by then expires instead of running late (60–86400)
queue.approval_ttl_hint: A request nobody approves or rejects by then expires (1–720)
queue.retention_hint: Only the encrypted original is wiped; the masked text stays for the audit trail (1–3650)
queue.confirm_retention: Turn on retention? Encrypted raw prompts older than this will be wiped permanently at the next sweep; the masked text and the audit trail stay.
queue.check_retention_hint: Verdicts of /actions/check older than this are deleted, except those an action or approval refers to (1–3650)
queue.content_retention_hint: Arguments, outputs, prompts and answers are erased; who did what, when and the verdict stay for the audit trail and the charts (1–3650)

byok.title: Encryption Keys
byok.hint: Connection keys, raw prompts and directory passwords are encrypted. With BYOK the organization gets its own data key, wrapped by a key you control - the server master key, your HashiCorp Vault or your AWS KMS. Revoke it on your side and Provenza can no longer read the data within 5 minutes; shred it here and nobody can.
byok.queued: Re-encryption runs in the background; refresh to follow it.
byok.confirm_disable: Turn BYOK off? All secrets are re-encrypted with the server key; the organization keys are retired.
byok.provider_local_hint: Per-organization key, rotation and shredding without an external service.
byok.provider_vault_transit_hint: The key encryption key never leaves your Vault.
byok.provider_aws_kms_hint: The key encryption key never leaves your AWS account; the organization is bound as encryption context.
byok.aws_missing: Needs boto3 on the server (pip install boto3).
byok.new_key_hint: A new data key is created, wrapped and unwrapped once to prove the key provider works, then every existing secret of the organization is re-encrypted with it. Secrets are stored encrypted; they are never shown again.
byok.confirm_rotate: Create a new data key and re-encrypt all secrets with it? The current key is retired but stays readable.
byok.confirm_enable: Enable BYOK and re-encrypt all secrets of the organization with its own key?
byok.shred_hint: Wipes every wrapped data key of the organization. Everything encrypted with them - connection keys, raw prompts, directory passwords - becomes unreadable for good. Values still on the server key are not affected. This cannot be undone.
byok.confirm_shred: Last chance: shred all organization keys? The data they protect will be lost permanently.

compliance.title: Compliance
compliance.hint: Requirements of the EU AI Act, GDPR, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF and the OWASP Agentic Top 10, checked against what Provenza actually knows. What only a person can confirm (documents, procedures) is attested here, with a link to the evidence. A pointer for orientation, not legal advice.
compliance.att_note: What was checked, by whom, where the evidence is
compliance.att_bad_url: Use an https:// link or a path in Provenza
compliance.reports_hint: A report is a frozen snapshot with a SHA-256 fingerprint; the report page checks that it was not altered and prints to PDF.
compliance.integrity_bad: CONTENT DOES NOT MATCH ITS FINGERPRINT
compliance.disclaimer: Generated by Provenza from its own records and recorded attestations. References are pointers for orientation, not legal advice.

obs.title: Agent observability
obs.hint: What your agents are doing right now: every policy decision and incident, streamed live. Only metadata is shown (agent, tool, verdict, guard codes, timing) — never arguments, outputs or reasons.
obs.no_data: No agent activity in this window.
obs.click_filter: Click to filter by this agent
obs.key_revoked_hint: This agent cannot call Provenza until a new key is issued

obs.reveal_hint: Admins only. Recorded in the audit log.

obs.unmasked: UNMASKED — recorded in the audit log
obs.no_events_window: no agent activity in the selected window

found.hint: AI agents found running on your devices: known products (coding agents, agent frameworks, agent platforms) and unrecognized programs that talk to an LLM API or load an LLM SDK. Nobody had to register them: review each one, then register it to put it under policies, or ignore it.

devices.title: Devices
devices.hint: Machines and browsers that report to Provenza, created automatically from the endpoint agent and the browser extension. A device is identified by its collector: the host name reported under an ingestion key.
devices.no_agents: No AI agents found on this device.
devices.empty_link: Create an ingestion key and install the endpoint agent.

enroll.issued_intro: Give this token to whoever runs the agent "{{name}}". It works once and expires {{time}}.
enroll.token_once: Shown only now. Only its hash is stored; issue a new one if it is lost.
enroll.command_hint: The tool generates the agent's keys on its own machine, proves possession by signing the server's challenge, and saves the keys and the agent's API key to provenza-agent.json (readable only by its owner). The private keys never leave that machine.

teams.title: Teams & Roles
teams.intro: Organization → team → sub-team → agent. A role template is a named set of rights: an agent with a role has exactly the role's capabilities, tools, models and delegation depth, and editing the role changes every agent that has it.
teams.name: Name
teams.roles_hint: An org-wide role can be given to any agent; a team's role only to that team's agents.
teams.require_hybrid_hint: Agents of this role must enroll with a hybrid key; agents with a classic key cannot be given it.
teams.require_attestation_hint: Agents of this role must prove where they run (a Kubernetes ServiceAccount token under the chosen policy) before they can act.
teams.confirm_role_update: This role is given to {{count}} agent(s). Their rights change with it. Continue?
teams.rights_from_role_hint: The agent gets the role's rights and keeps them in step with the role.
teams.create_teams_hint: No teams yet — create them under Teams & Roles.
teams.agent_rights_from_role: Rights come from the role; change the role to change them.
teams.assign_role_hint: The agent's rights will be replaced by the role's.
teams.unassign_role_hint: Without a role the agent keeps its current rights, editable per agent.

attest.title: Workload attestation
attest.intro: Agents whose role requires attestation must prove where they run before they can act: the agent sends its pod's Kubernetes ServiceAccount token, signed with its own key over a fresh challenge. The token must come from your cluster, for the audience below, from an allowed namespace or service account, and be bound to a pod. A passing attestation lasts for the policy's validity (never past the token's own expiry); the agent repeats it on a schedule.
attest.name: Name
attest.audience_hint: Must be the same in the pod spec (serviceAccountToken.audience), here and in the token. Use a value only Provenza accepts, never the API server's.
attest.jwks_discovery: OIDC discovery on the issuer (public issuer)
attest.jwks_keep: Leave empty to keep the stored keys
attest.jwks_discovery_hint: Provenza reads {issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration and the keys it names, and caches both for an hour.
attest.jwks_not_json: The keys are not valid JSON.
attest.rules_hint: Patterns with * are allowed. A token passes when its namespace OR its namespace/service account matches. At least one rule is required.
attest.require_pod_hint: Projected tokens are bound to their pod; long-lived Secret tokens are not and are refused.
attest.validity_hint: After this the agent must attest again with a fresh token.
attest.confirm_update: Roles use this policy: their agents' current attestations stop counting until they attest again. Continue?
attest.setup_pod: 1. Give the agent's pod a projected token for this audience
attest.setup_agent: 2. Run next to the agent (sidecar or background loop)
attest.setup_agent_hint: It re-reads the token each time (the kubelet renews it) and attests before the previous attestation lapses.
attest.setup_roles: 3. In a role template, turn on "Require attestation" and pick this policy:
attest.test_hint: e.g. kubectl create token <sa> -n <namespace> --audience <audience> - checked against the policy, nothing is recorded.
attest.enroll_hint: This agent's role requires attestation (policy "{{policy}}"): it can act only after proving where it runs. Its pod needs a projected ServiceAccount token for audience "{{audience}}", and the agent must run:
attest.jwks_url_required: Enter the URL of the cluster's keys.

ph.title: Policy hierarchy
ph.intro: One policy at three levels: organization → team (and its sub-teams) → agent. A lower level can only tighten what is above it: the smallest limit wins, every level's allow list must allow, all deny and approval lists apply, and a switch turned on anywhere stays on. It applies to the gateway, to agent actions and - the organization level - to user requests.
ph.every_level_must_allow: each level listed must allow it
ph.ignored: No effect (a level above is stricter)
ph.confirm_clear: Remove every rule of this level? The change is kept in the audit log.
ph.fix_yaml_first: Fix the YAML first - it cannot be shown as a form while it has errors.
ph.form_hint: Lists: comma-separated, * allowed (kb.*). An empty field sets nothing at this level. To allow nothing at all, write `allow: []` in YAML.
ph.scope_hint_org: Applies to every agent, every gateway call and every user request of the organization.
ph.scope_hint_team: Applies to the team's agents and to its sub-teams, on top of the organization level.
ph.scope_hint_agent: Applies to this agent only, on top of its team and the organization.
ph.org_effective_hint: Agents see this plus their team and own levels; user requests see the organization level (without the gateway settings).
ph.agent_effective_link: Policy levels that apply to this agent
ph.yaml_only: This level has an empty allow list (allow nothing), which the form cannot show - edit it as YAML.
ph.terms_moved: Blocked terms are kept on their own page, with the same levels (organization, team, agent):

ks.title: Kill switch
ks.intro: Stop AI in steps: one agent, a team (with its sub-teams), every agent, or all of the organization's AI traffic. Each stop needs a reason, is recorded with who and when, and is lifted on its own: lifting gives back exactly what that stop stopped - agents stopped earlier for other reasons stay stopped.
ks.load_failed: Could not load the kill switch
ks.traffic_note: The gateway and AI requests (including the playground) are refused while this stop is in force, and requests already queued fail - send them again after the stop is lifted. Agents created meanwhile start suspended.
ks.lift_explain: Lifting switches back on the {{count}} agent(s) this stop suspended, unless another stop still holds them (that stop then gives them back) or they changed since. Ended delegation chains are not resumed.

what.agent: One agent is suspended and its delegation chains end.
what.team: Every agent of a team and its sub-teams is suspended.
what.all_agents: Every agent of the organization; new agents start suspended.
what.org_traffic: Every agent, plus the gateway and AI requests of all users.

ks.reason_ph: What happened - it goes to the audit log and the history
ks.terminate_chains_hint: Work the agents passed on to other agents stops too. Ended chains are not resumed when the stop is lifted.

warn.all_agents: Every agent of the organization stops at once, and stays stopped until this stop is lifted.
warn.org_traffic: Every agent stops, and the gateway and AI requests of all users are refused until this stop is lifted; requests already queued fail.

ks.confirm_team: Stop every agent of team {{name}} and its sub-teams now?
ks.stopped_notice: Stopped: {{agents}} agent(s) suspended, {{chains}} delegation chain(s) ended.
ks.lifted_notice: Lifted: {{restored}} agent(s) switched back on, {{kept}} still held by another stop, {{skipped}} left as they are.

pii.title: PII rules
pii.intro: What the Prompt Firewall looks for before a prompt leaves - in the gateway, user AI requests and the playground - and what it does: mask the value as [MASKED:TYPE], or block the whole prompt. Your own patterns are checked first, so an identifier they catch is not reported as something else. Masked views of stored text (observability) use the same rules, where block only masks.
pii.load_failed: Could not load the PII rules
pii.saved: Saved. The firewall uses it from the next prompt.
pii.names_ner: Names: NER model ({{langs}}) and the Uzbek gazetteer
pii.names_no_ner: Names: Uzbek gazetteer only - no NER model is configured
pii.name: Name
pii.label: Label
pii.label_hint: Shown in masked text as [MASKED:{{label}}]. A-Z, 0-9, _.
pii.pattern_hint: Checked before saving: no back references, no repetition inside a repetition like (a+)+, no alternatives inside a repetition like (a|aa)+, no open-ended .* or [^…]+ (use {0,50}), and it must run fast on long text. Use \b for word boundaries.
pii.rule_deleted: Rule removed (kept in the audit log).
pii.no_rules: No rules of your own yet.
pii.timeouts: Ran out of time {{count}} time(s) - those prompts were refused. Simplify the pattern.

pii.sample_hint: Runs through the firewall with the current settings (and the rule being edited). Nothing is stored.

bt.title: Blocked terms
bt.intro: Words a prompt must not contain - project code names, client names, confidential markers - in one place. Each term says where it applies, how it is found and what happens: Block refuses the prompt, Monitor lets it through and records that the term was seen (try a new term in Monitor before blocking). Whole-word matching sees through the usual disguises: P r o j e c t, Project_Titan, Pr0ject, look-alike Cyrillic letters, invisible characters.
bt.load_failed: Could not load the blocked terms
bt.match_hint_word: Finds the term as whole words, also written apart, joined, with _ or -, digits for letters (0 for o), look-alike letters of other scripts or accents. "ass" does not find "class".
bt.match_hint_substring: Finds the term's letters anywhere, also inside other words: "titan" finds "titanium".

scope_hint.agent: This agent's calls through the gateway.
scope_hint.policy: User requests of use cases governed by this policy, and the playground while the policy is active.
